A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CaseFacts. All 19 pages of v1 and 20 pages of v2, including their appendices, support comparison. Figures, tables, and prompts can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original dataset analyses, human verification, GPT-4o baseline evaluations, and embedding-model fine-tuning results.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds retrieval comparators, annotation agreement, attorney review, and judge-reliability and identifier analyses.

M1.justification: The claim-generation, validation, similarity-filtering, and negation pipeline remains unchanged, as does the embedding fine-tuning objective. The expanded threshold explanation and new pipeline figure describe existing procedures; all 14 appendix prompts are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the reported 6,294-claim benchmark, 3,299 Oyez Supreme Court cases, and the same retrieval and three-verdict tasks. The added validation and identifier-subset analyses examine existing coverage without introducing another corpus or task domain.

E2.justification: V2 Table 6 adds evaluated BM25 and ColBERT retrieval comparators alongside BGE, MiniLM, and Qwen. The GPT-4o Naive and Search comparator pair remains unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 evaluates Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B after five epochs, which v1 explicitly omitted. It also introduces procedures for the attorney review, judge-reliability evaluation, and identifier-subset comparison. The retained experiments report the same splits, metrics, and baseline settings.

E4.justification: V2 substantially extends dataset-quality checks: Section 3.5 evaluates factuality, contradiction, and overlap judgments against human-annotated test data; Section 3.6 audits identifying entities and compares subset performance. Section 2.4 additionally reports an independent attorney review of 50 claims. These address reliability and potential evaluation shortcuts beyond v1's retained analyses.

E5.justification: Section 2.4 newly reports a 100-claim overlap between annotators and Cohen's kappa of 0.637. This adds agreement estimation, without establishing an increase in annotation effort or repeated model runs.

E6.justification: Tables 5 and 6 extensively replace scores under retained stated settings. Naive/Search Verdict Scores change from 0.260/0.228 to 0.185/0.169; one-epoch Qwen Recall@1 changes from 0.6440 to 0.4999. V2 adds comparator, five-epoch Qwen, and validation results, including Table 7 judge accuracies of 97.4%, 95.5%, and 97.4%. The factuality table also corrects 1,483 inconsistent claims to 1,484. The PDFs do not explain the wholesale score revisions.

T1.justification: The task formulation, verdict definitions, and Evidence Score and Verdict Score definitions remain unchanged. Neither version adds theorems, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion match, and the contribution statements retain their scope: colloquial legal verification, explicit overruling labels, scalable synthetic-data construction, and challenging evidence retrieval. Added validation supports these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: V2 newly interprets judge results as alignment with human judgment and residual identifying entities as having negligible benchmark impact while improving realism. It removes the earlier rationale for omitting five-epoch Qwen evaluation. The limitations section and interpretation of web-search failures remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 explicitly identifies cosine similarity and names roberta-large-ner-english for the new identifier audit. The main release link changes from the supreme-court-dataset repository to CaseFacts, although Appendix A.1 retains the former address. Existing prompts and generation hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds COLIEE and positions it as formal-to-formal retrieval and entailment, contrasting with CaseFacts' colloquial claims. It also replaces the Anand et al. 2022 survey citation with the distinct 2023 Explainable Information Retrieval publication. Most other reference changes update formatting or publication metadata.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized language corrections, expands the threshold-selection explanation, adds Sections 3.5 and 3.6, and removes an author affiliation footnote. The overall narrative structure, abstract, conclusion, limitations, and appendix text remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adds the pipeline diagram as Figure 1 and judge-evaluation Table 7, relocates the similarity table, and reformats several tables. Table 6 becomes more compact and changes its highlighting convention. The original length-distribution figure is retained as Figure 2, and the prompt layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The newly reported annotator agreement and independent 50-claim attorney review provide useful evidence about label quality that v1 lacked. Additional retrieval comparators improve benchmark context. The gain is limited by unexplained score replacements and reporting inconsistencies: Section 3.6 gives a full-test Evidence Score of 0.222, whereas Table 5 reports 0.232, and the steady-training-gains discussion does not fully match Table 6.
